quote.text: Neither worse then or better is a thing made by being praised.
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize that the true value of nurturing lies not in the praise you receive, but in the genuine growth and character you help shape in your children; let your actions, rather than third-party approval, guide your parenting.
    • Teach your children to seek internal worth over external validation, so they understand that consistent virtues and integrity are far more enduring than transient accolades.
  • Leadership
    • Emphasize that the measure of a leader's worth is found in steadfast principles and wisdom, not in the fleeting applause of followers; consistent ethical conduct forms the basis of true leadership.
    • Encourage a focus on self-improvement and accountability, understanding that external praise should be regarded as a byproduct rather than the goal of leadership, which must be rooted in service and virtue.
  • Product Management
    • In product management, allow your decisions to be guided by intrinsic quality and customer satisfaction rather than the temporary allure of external praise; a well-founded product naturally earns genuine respect over time.
    • Consider criticism and accolades alike as data points; focus on the substance and long-term impact of your products rather than on the superficial validations which may distract you from continuous improvement.
